message.content:
Sure! Here’s a quick rundown of appliances that can bake a chocolate cake (and a bit about when each one shines):

| Machine | Why it works for chocolate cake | Best use case |
|---------|---------------------------------|---------------|
| **Standard electric or gas oven** | Classic choice – gives even heat and a nice rise. | Any size cake; best for traditional baking. |
| **Convection oven** | Fan circulates hot air, baking faster and more evenly. | When you want a crisp top and a shorter bake time. |
| **Toaster oven** | Compact, great for small cakes or cupcakes. | Quick, single-serving cakes or when you don’t want to heat a full oven. |
| **Microwave oven** | Uses microwave energy to heat quickly. | “Microwave mug cakes” or very quick, single-serving cakes. |
| **Cake maker / cake pan** | Dedicated appliance or pan that can be used in an oven or microwave. | When you want a consistent shape and size without a full oven. |
| **Bread machine** | Many models have a “cake” setting. | Convenient for small batches; no need to preheat an oven. |
| **Slow cooker** | Uses low, steady heat; can produce a moist cake. | When you want a cake that stays soft and moist. |
| **Pressure cooker** | Can bake cakes quickly under pressure. | For a quick, moist cake when you’re short on time. |
| **Sous vide** | Precise temperature control; can bake a cake in a sealed bag. | For a very even bake and a unique texture. |

**Bottom line:**  
- If you’re looking for the most reliable, go with a **standard or convection oven**.  
- For a quick, single-serving treat, a **microwave** or **toaster oven** works well.  
- If you want a specialized appliance, a **cake maker** or **bread machine** can simplify the process.

Let me know if you’d like a recipe or more details on any particular appliance!
